newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaeuble urges no delay to German tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: Schaeuble urges no delay to German tax reforms.

text.p: Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, called on Friday for a new round of talks with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to take place next week.
Schaeuble told parliament that the three-party ruling coalition was ready to resume talks at any time. "There must be no delay to decisions on tax reforms," he said.

Schaeuble's remarks were the latest in a flurry of public comments by government and SPD politicians seeking to probe the other side's willingness to talk again on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to cut 30 billion marks in taxes.

The SPD walked out of cross-party negotiations a week ago in sympathy with miners protesting at government plans to cut coal subsidies. But that row was settled on Thursday, leaving the way open to a possible resumption of talks.
SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Thursday the government must come up with new proposals to relieve the tax load on ordinary workers and families from the start of next year.

But his party lieutenants appeared to offer a softer line on Friday, with finance spokeswoman Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier saying a compromise was possible if Waigel did not stick doggedly to his plan to slash top-rate income tax.
Waigel was due to unveil a legislative draft of his tax reforms at a news conference at 1100 GMT on Friday.
Schaeuble underlined the commitment of the coalition to the tax reforms, saying that its main goal should be to boost investment.
"Tax rates must be cut -- that's the only way we can fight unemployment," he told the Bundestag lower house. Unemployment stood at a post-war record 4.7 million in February.
He added that the SPD's strategy of putting more cash in consumers' pockets to boost domestic demand would fail to hit its target of cutting joblessness.
The two sides, he said, were not far apart on cutting Germany's notoriously high labour overheads.
